text:
I’ll inspect the repository structure and its SEO-relevant surfaces (metadata, routing, sitemap/robots, structured data, content, and rendering), then report only actionable findings with exact file and line references.

**Static audit:** the main SEO blockers are the staging canonical URL, contradictory indexing directives, invalid structured data, and thin entity/content signals for AI search.

| Priority | File and line | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 Critical | `src/_includes/base.njk:8` | Every page canonicalizes to `staging.brightside-dental.example`, while the sitemap and configured origin use `www.brightside-dental.example`. | Generate canonicals from the production site origin; never hardcode the staging hostname. |
| 🔴 Critical | `src/services.njk:5`, `src/sitemap.xml:5` | `/services/` is marked `noindex` but is included in the XML sitemap and prominently linked in navigation. | Remove `noindex` if it is an SEO landing page; otherwise remove it from the sitemap and navigation. |
| 🔴 Critical | `src/contact.njk:9-11` | JSON-LD is invalid JSON because of the trailing comma after the telephone value, so search engines can ignore the entire schema block. | Remove the trailing comma and validate the generated structured data. |
| 🟠 High | `src/contact.njk:10` | The `Dentist` entity lacks useful local-business fields such as `address`, `url`, `image`, `openingHours`, and `sameAs`. This weakens local SEO and AI entity resolution. | Add complete, accurate `Dentist`/`LocalBusiness` structured data, including the production URL and physical address. |
| 🟠 High | `src/team.njk:1-6` | The page has no meta description and contains no dentist names, credentials, specialties, profile links, or individual expertise. This is weak E-E-A-T and poor source material for AI answers. | Add a description and detailed provider profiles with names, qualifications, specialties, and relevant links. |
| 🟠 High | `src/services.njk:7-9` | Services are only a short list with no treatment-specific explanations, eligibility, process, pricing context, FAQs, or location relevance. AI systems have little quotable information. | Create substantive sections or dedicated pages for each service with clear answers to patient questions. |
| 🟡 Medium | `src/_includes/base.njk:2` | The document has no language attribute, reducing explicit language/locale signaling. | Use `<html lang="en-GB">`. |
| 🟡 Medium | `src/_includes/base.njk:6-9` | No Open Graph or Twitter metadata is emitted, reducing link-preview quality and share-discovery signals. | Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:type`, `og:image`, and equivalent Twitter metadata. |
| 🟡 Medium | `src/index.njk:8` | The page references `/img/reception.jpg`, but no image asset exists in the repository, producing a broken image in the built site. | Add the image or remove/update the reference; provide a stable, optimized image URL for social/schema use. |
| 🟡 Medium | `src/contact.njk:8` | `data-nosnippet` hides the insurance statement from search snippets. If this is useful patient-facing factual content, it also reduces extractable context for AI search systems. | Remove `data-nosnippet` unless suppressing this information is intentional. |
| 🟡 Medium | `src/contact.njk:6-7`, `src/geo.config.json:1` | Business identity is not consistently represented in visible content and structured data: the address/phone appear only on Contact, while the configured origin is not wired into templates. | Centralize business data and expose consistent name, address, phone, service area, and URL across the site and schema. |

`src/robots.txt` allows crawling and references the production sitemap, which is appropriate, but it does not compensate for the canonical mismatch or the sitemap/noindex conflict.
